added.description: The Research.md R5 row says R5 states it as a conflict if the display does not isolate its VBUS. FU-2I and FU-2F returned it: the display's Type_C2 VBUS joins its 5V net with only a TVS to ground (V80, found: 'No'), so link power from the TPS259474ARPWR reaches the VBUS pin of the display's native USB-C socket and back-feeds a host or charger plugged there. The IO board side blocks reverse current (V266), which does not stop the forward feed. Connecting both at once is not specified as safe. P5 returned no entry for it.

added.kind: PIO bind order: programming mode refused
added.description: Combination 'every mix ... 68 of 81' says a port in a programming mode is allocated as 2 state machines and at most 16 words. pico-sdk 2.3.0 pio.c:454-508 does not reserve a port's freed space: a PIO UART bound with the same call as out_dshot.c (tx 4 words, rx 9 words, one pin) is placed where it finds a free state machine, and a block that holds PPM first stays at GPIO base 0 and cannot take pins 32 and up. A port that was bidirectional always rebinds. Programming binds that happen before the 4 ports and the socket (combination 'all four in programming mode') fit: 11 state machines, 69 words.
